channel.title: Web3 Hub
channel.description: Web3 Hub reports crypto news: Bitcoin and Ethereum, exchanges, DeFi protocols, stablecoins, regulation, security incidents and network upgrades.

item.title: How Treasury Teams Reconcile Cross-Chain Swap Amounts
item.description: Treasury teams should match each swap’s source debit to its destination credit, isolate chain and protocol fees, and preserve a transaction trail for valuation and audit.

item.title: Lower Gas or More Output? Compare the Net Value
item.description: Lower-gas swap routes can leave more value after fees, while higher-output routes can win when fees are small; compare both in the asset you will spend.

item.title: Token Contract Replacements Need a Plan for Every Chain
item.description: Replacing a token contract means deploying a new version on each chain, then migrating balances or routing future activity through a chain-specific process.

item.title: Why Cross-Chain Swaps Split Across Pools
item.description: A cross-chain swap may use several pools to improve its exchange rate, but each route adds fees, execution steps and failure points to compare.

item.title: Five Steps to Buy Fractional NFT Shares on Mantle
item.description: Buying fractional NFT shares on Mantle takes five checks: confirm the share token, bridge a supported payment asset, reserve gas, and read the vault’s exit rules.

item.title: A Cross-Chain Swap Is Pending During a Network Halt: What to Do
item.description: If a network in your cross-chain swap has halted, wait for it to resume and check the transaction on that chain before trying again. A halt can pause one…

item.title: Why a destination swap can fail after a bridge
item.description: A failed destination swap can leave bridged tokens on the receiving chain; check both transaction records and the token balance before retrying or sending funds again.

item.title: Track a Crypto Transfer at Both Wallets
item.description: A transfer is complete only when the network confirms it and the receiving wallet credits it; track the sender record, transaction ID and destination balance.

item.title: How to Send Native Crypto Without a Token Approval
item.description: Native coins move in a signed transaction, while token approvals let contracts spend ERC-20 balances; the distinction changes the steps and permissions on-chain.

item.title: Why Cross-Chain Swaps Deduct Gas From Your Payout
item.description: Cross-chain swaps may subtract destination gas from the output because the service pays the receiving chain fee; check the net amount, fee basis and quote expiry.

item.title: How to Clear a Pending Mantle Bridge Wallet Nonce
item.description: A stuck Mantle Bridge transaction usually needs a same-network replacement at the blocked nonce; clearing wallet activity alone does not cancel an on-chain transaction.

item.title: Four Checks to Make on a Pending Cross-Chain Swap
item.description: A pending cross-chain swap is a sequence of transactions. Check the source receipt, bridge status, destination execution and final token balance to find its hold-up.

item.title: Read the destination amount before you bridge
item.description: A bridge quote’s destination amount is the number to compare: check the output token, route fees, slippage floor and network costs before signing.

item.title: Permit signatures can remove a separate token approval
item.description: Permit signatures move token approval into a wallet message, letting a swap contract use it in the same transaction when the token and route support permits.

item.title: Cross-chain payouts trade speed for simpler treasury settlement
item.description: Recurring cross-chain payouts settle per payment or through treasury batches, trading recipient speed for fewer transactions and simpler destination-chain operations.

item.title: What Happens When You Bridge Crypto to Another Chain?
item.description: A bridge moves value between chains by locking, minting or releasing tokens, but timing, fees and trust depend on its design and the destination network.

item.title: Bridge Stablecoins Before Paying a Cross-Chain Invoice
item.description: Match the invoice’s network, token and amount before bridging; compare route time and fees, then verify the destination balance before sending payment.

item.title: Keep Gas on Both Chains Before Your First Cross-Chain Swap
item.description: A cross-chain swap can require gas on more than one network. Keep each chain’s native token available for the route and any follow-up transaction.

item.title: Ledger details implant attack on CryptoBilis wallet sales
item.description: Ledger says a hidden implant in CryptoBilis-sold wallets read 24-word recovery phrases and sent them over LTE; it is tightening reseller checks as the inquiry continues.

item.title: Check Destination Gas Before You Bridge Crypto
item.description: A bridge can move tokens without funding the destination network’s fees; check the delivery mode, gas token and wallet balance before you start each time.
